Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: The absolutive is zero-marked; the agentive marker le³³ marks only transitive A and Sa (agentive intransitive S).
curated_comment: Lisu, Central/Lipo dialect (hual1240, ISO lis, Sino-Tibetan/Tibeto-Burman, Yunnan China) — Language and family corrected: original xlsx listed 'VERIFICAR (PDF apunta a Lisu, no a Hualapai)'; PDF is Yu (2007), a comprehensive grammar of Lisu. hual1240 corresponds to the Central/Lipo dialect variety. The language has an active-stative (split-S) system: the agentive marker le³³ marks transitive A and agentive intransitive Sa, while non-agentive So takes zero. This is NOT a pure ergative system. CRITICAL CORRECTION: GB409_24 changed 1→0. The original annotation incorrectly identified nɛ³³ as the ergative/instrumental marker; PDF verification confirms nɛ³³ is the LOCATIVE marker in Central Lisu (demonstrative in other dialects). The actual ergative/agentive marker is le³³; instrumental is du³³. Other changes: GB409_11 ?→1 (non-indicative moods use le³³), GB409_19 1→? (inanimate A uncertain). Glottocode hual1240 is correct (Lipo/Central Lisu variety); the previously proposed lisu1250 corresponds to the broader Lisu dialect cluster.

Comment: Full NPs take the agentive marker le³³ in transitive clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative/agentive marker le³³ is not restricted by aspect; appears in imperfective contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Ergative/agentive marker le³³ appears in perfective contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: le³³ is present in past tense contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: le³³ is present in non-past (present/future) contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: le³³ appears in indicative clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: le³³ appears in non-indicative moods (imperative/optative). Confirmed from Yu (2007); changed from original annotation '?'→1.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: le³³ appears in realis contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: le³³ appears in irrealis contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Agentive/volitional A takes le³³ (Sa in active-stative system).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Non-agentive intransitive S (So) takes the absolutive (zero mark), not le³³. The active-stative (split-S) system distinguishes Sa (agentive, takes le³³) from So (non-agentive, takes zero). Non-agentive A is not clearly attested as a distinct class; value 0 reflects the So system.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: In the active-stative system, the key distinction is agentivity/control, not topicality. Non-agentive S (So) and O pattern together (absolutive). Topical A does not systematically lose le³³. GB409_16=0 indicates no topicality conditioning on ergative marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: Non-topical A takes le³³ as expected.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Animate A takes le³³.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Inanimate A: no clear examples found in Yu (2007) for Central Lisu dialect; inanimate entities rarely appear as transitive agents in the documented corpus. Value uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: le³³ appears in main clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Non-main clauses: insufficient documentation in Yu (2007) to confirm or deny ergative marking in subordinate constructions for this dialect.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative alignment is conditioned by the active-stative (split-S) distinction: agentive/volitional Sa takes le³³, non-agentive So takes zero. This semantic/agentivity conditioning constitutes additional conditioning beyond basic transitivity.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The ergative marker le³³ and the genitive marker are distinct.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: CORRECTED from original annotation 1→0. Original annotation cited nɛ³³ as both ergative and instrumental, but PDF verification (Yu 2007) confirms that nɛ³³ is the LOCATIVE marker in Central Lisu, not instrumental. The agentive/ergative marker is le³³; the instrumental marker is du³³. ERG≠INST.
